categoryNotes.zht: 刺史初為監察郡國之職，然其職權漸重，後多兼領行政，實與州牧相類。自西漢末，刺史可開府，自行徵辟掾吏。其所辟之屬，多不獨奉天子為君，亦以徵辟己之刺史為「君」，遂成錢穆所謂「二重君主观」。
categoryNotes.zhs: 刺史初为监察郡国之职，然其职权渐重，后多兼领行政，实与州牧相类。自西汉末，刺史可开府，自行征辟掾吏。其所辟之属，多不独奉天子为君，亦以征辟己之刺史为'君'，遂成钱穆所谓'二重君主观'。
categoryNotes.en: Originally, the inspector served as a supervisory official charged with monitoring commanderies and states. Over time, however, the authority of the office steadily expanded, and inspectors frequently came to exercise administrative powers as well, effectively resembling provincial governors. From the late Western (Former) Han onward, inspectors were allowed to establish their own office and appoint subordinate officials on their own authority.

Those appointed under such arrangements would not view the emperor as their sole sovereign; they would also treat the inspector who had recruited them as their 'lord.' This situation gave rise to what Qian Mu famously described as a system of 'dual allegiance.'

categoryNotes.zht: 郡守與刺史相類，其屬吏除丞、尉由朝廷任命外，亦皆可開府自行徵辟署置。郡吏除去京畿及邊郡，例用本籍之人，所辟者亦多奉郡守為「君」，具「二重君主观」。郡守雖不能隨意更調朝廷所置之縣令，然可暫置守令以代理縣事。郡守可自設條教以化民俗、理民生；兼掌賞罰、司法，乃至生殺予奪。郡守任滿一歲則亦有選舉之權，可舉賢良方正、歲貢等。
categoryNotes.zhs: 郡守与刺史相类，其属吏除丞、尉由朝廷任命外，皆可开府自行征辟署置。郡吏除京畿及边郡外，例用本籍之人，所辟者亦多奉郡守为'君'，具'二重君主'。郡守虽不能随意更调朝廷所置之县令，然可暂置守令以代理县事。郡守可自设条教以化民俗、理民生；兼掌赏罚、司法，乃至生杀予夺。郡守任满一岁则亦有选举之权，可举贤良方正、岁贡等。
categoryNotes.en: Commandery administrators were similar to inspectors in establishing offices. With the exception of the Commandery Assistant and Commandant, who were appointed by the central court, all subordinate officials could likewise be recruited and appointed at the Administrator's discretion. Other than the capital region and border commanderies, commandery officials were customarily drawn from the local populace. Those so appointed often regarded the Administrator as their 'lord' as well, thus also exhibiting 'dual allegiance.'

categoryNotes.zht: 漢制，本郡稅賦歸於朝廷，郡國用度由朝廷撥付，邊郡資用不足則由內郡調濟支應。郡守亦須於秋冬課核屬吏，由屬縣先期集課，郡覆核之，并於正月彙總上計於朝廷。
categoryNotes.zhs: 汉制，本郡税赋归于朝廷，郡国用度由朝廷拨付，边郡资用不足则由内郡调济支应。郡守亦须于秋冬课核属吏，由属县先期集课，郡复核之，并于正月汇总上计于朝廷。
categoryNotes.en: Although an administrator could not arbitrarily remove county magistrates appointed by the court, he was permitted to appoint acting magistrates to manage county affairs on a temporary basis. An administrator could promulgate local ordinances to guide local customs and regulate livelihoods, exercise authority over rewards and punishments, oversee judicial matters, and, in extreme cases, wield the power to execute. After serving one full year, the administrator also gains the right to make recommendations, including nominations for Filial and Incorrupt, and Worthy and Upright candidates, as well as annual recommendations.

Under the Han system, taxes collected within a commandery were remitted to the capital, and local expenditures allocated back by the central government. Border commanderies whose revenues proved insufficient were subsidized through transfers from interior commanderies. Commandery administrators were also required to evaluate their subordinate officials in autumn-winter. Preliminary assessments were conducted at the county level, reviewed at the commandery level, and then compiled into annual reports submitted to the court in the first month of the year.

categoryNotes.zht: 漢魏皆沿秦制，縣下設鄉、里為戶籍單位。鄉內又以亭部作地域劃分，與里並行，以十里（長度單位，~4km）為一亭，設亭所，築門牆、樓室，掌文書傳遞、察姦捕盜等，兼供過路者住宿之便。十亭部為一鄉，治所所在之亭，則稱「都亭」。
categoryNotes.zhs: 汉魏皆沿秦制，县下设乡、里为户籍单位。乡内又以亭部作地域划分，与里并行，以十里（长度单位，约4公里）为一亭，设亭所，筑门墙、楼室，掌文书传递、察奸捕盗等，兼供过路者住宿之便。十亭部为一乡，治所所在之亭，则称'都亭'。
categoryNotes.en: Both the Han and Wei dynasties followed Qin administrative practice in organizing households below the county level into townships and villages as units of household registration. Within each township, neighborhood stations were also established as territorial divisions, operating alongside villages. Neighborhood stations were laid out at intervals of ten li (~4 km). Each station was a walled compound with gates and buildings, responsible for functions like relaying official communications, suppressing crime, and providing lodging for travelers. Ten such neighborhood stations constituted a township; the station where the township seat was located would be known as the capital neighborhood station.
